source.title: Interpreting GFlowNets for Drug Discovery: What probes can and cannot show
source.authors: S. AmirthaVarshiniA; D. Ranasinghe; H. Tam

record.file_problem: No apparent garbling or truncation. The paper states that the analyzed SynFlowNet checkpoint is unavailable; extracted embeddings are the surviving artifact.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests cross-seed reproducibility of SAE dictionary directions and finds that most are near chance, qualifying claims that SAE features are stable, portable units.
record.gate_note: The paper discusses features held in superposition as motivation, but does not test toy-model superposition, feature competition for network capacity, LLM representations, or one-dimensional versus multidimensional feature geometry. The SAE reconstruction and cross-seed stability results bear on V5. Probe decoding, motif results, saliency, and property-specific probe ablations do not establish the other claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study trains overcomplete BatchTopK SAEs on frozen embeddings from a graph-transformer policy (SynFlowNet). It measures reconstruction and information retention, which bear on completeness, and cross-seed decoder matching, which bears on stability. Most features reproduce near chance, so V5's stability claim needs qualifying in this non-LLM setting.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors call their most important result a negative control: an untrained network of identical architecture decodes every property about as well as the trained policy, so probe decodability reflects architecture and featurization. They claim the overcomplete SAE is a good exact-sparsity decomposition with chemically enriched detectors in individual runs. Only a small subset of directions is stable across seeds, so they restrict feature-level claims to that reproducible core.
record.recipe_differences: The study applies undercomplete and overcomplete SAEs to frozen SynFlowNet molecular embeddings; it does not reproduce the original toy-network experiments or their feature-geometry measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Cross-seed matching shows that feature reproducibility depends on the SAE run: most directions are near chance, while a small subset is above the stated thresholds.

fits_no_version.finding: An overcomplete SAE on a molecular graph transformer's embeddings recovers sparse, chemically enriched detectors: per-halogen, boron, and benzene-absence features. Single-feature ablations have property-specific effects on probe decoding (8–23× specificity).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAEs recover sparse, interpretable features in non-language models (graph transformers), analogous to V4 but outside LLMs.

record.problems: The analyzed trained checkpoint no longer exists. The study reports that only a small subset of SAE directions is stable across seeds. Reconstruction quality is not a test of semantic canonicity. The untrained-network control used a single random initialization, though it is not central to the feature-stability result.
record.rows_left_out: No other results were omitted for the 60-row limit. Probe decoding, motif detection, saliency, and probe-ablation outcomes are not rows because they do not test the claim versions' superposition or canonical-unit assertions.

untested.parts: All of it: toy networks, the sparsity-dependent phase transition, and feature geometry.
Capacity competition as the cause of polysemanticity.
Non-capacity origins of polysemantic neurons. The paper explicitly declines to read its multi-target counts as polysemanticity.
Canonicity, i.e. whether features are the model's semantic units. Stability across dictionary sizes. Whether features persist on untrained-network embeddings (stated as untested).

missing.what: Information retention through the SAE bottleneck: median 98.3%, worst case flexibility at 83%, and QED improved by +0.033 in the latent. This bears on V5 completeness.
The hyperparameter sweep shows SAE outcomes depend on configuration. ReLU+ℓ1 gives L0 > 500; BatchTopK with k = 8 or 16 gives 85–97% dead features.

record.verdict_notes: The subject is a graph transformer, not an LLM; V5 is treated as model-general. Not an original source. The analyzed checkpoint is lost; the results come from the saved embeddings. The labels split completeness (supported) from stability (limited to a small core). The 'challenges' label was considered for stability, because the bulk of the dictionary sits at chance.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-network superposition, sparse features exceeding network dimensions, near-orthogonal overlap, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether neuron polysemanticity is caused by limited-capacity competition or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise for reasons other than capacity pressure.
Feature spreading or sparse feature recovery in LLMs.
Cross-seed stability and embedding reconstruction are tested. The study does not establish that SAE features are canonical semantic units or a complete account of the model's representation.
Whether represented features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional features.

rows.subject: SynFlowNet (frozen embeddings; analyzed checkpoint unavailable)
rows.operation_detail: Measured embedding reconstruction NMSE using a 4× overcomplete BatchTopK SAE.
rows.note: The authors report that this is a 1.75× better reconstruction than the matched 256 → 128 linear baseline at comparable average activity. Reconstruction quality does not by itself establish canonical semantic units.
rows.check: Only the completeness part of V5 is addressed. NMSE of 0.00151 means near-complete reconstruction. The baseline shown is a different SAE architecture, not a control for the version.

conditions.value: 256 → 128, single linear layer each way, ℓ1
identical split and seeds to the overcomplete model

rows.note: This baseline reconstructs less well than the overcomplete SAE; the paper notes that the models differ in both width and sparsity mechanism.
rows.check: This is a comparator method (a 256→128 linear ℓ1 SAE), not a measurement of V5. The 'partial' state is meaningless here. The paper notes the two SAEs differ in both width and sparsity mechanism.

rows.subject: SynFlowNet (frozen embeddings; analyzed checkpoint unavailable)
rows.operation_detail: Matched decoder columns across independently seeded SAE runs and compared their cosine similarity with a random-dictionary chance baseline.
rows.measure: Mean best-match decoder-column cosine; fractions exceeding stated cosine thresholds
rows.value: Mean best-match cosine 0.237 (1.11× chance); 2.71% of features exceed cosine 0.5 and 0.97% exceed 0.7
rows.note: The paper says the bulk of the dictionary is at chance, while a small core exceeds thresholds that no random pair attains; it concludes that feature indices are not portable across runs.
rows.check: Mean best-match cosine is 0.237 against 0.214 for chance (1.11×). Only 2.71% of features exceed 0.5 and 0.97% exceed 0.7. Stability holds only for a tiny core; the bulk is near absent.
